src/opengrad/evaluation/candidate.py::co.reason: candidate.py imports yaml, the experiment store and env_capture; whole-file vendoring would pull a training-lifecycle subsystem into a benchmark package.

modification_policy: Never edited. If a vendored function is wrong, the finding is reported upstream and this benchmark reports the upstream behaviour intact, because a score produced by a divergent copy is not comparable to an OpenGrad score.
not_vendored: src/opengrad/evaluation/runner.py -- its InferenceBackend protocol passes CanonicalEvaluationExample to the backend, exposing expected_decision. toolchoice.harness.protocol uses the benchmarks-side shape instead.
src/opengrad/data/renderers.py -- prompt rendering is model-specific and is reimplemented in toolchoice.harness.prompt against the published chat template.

opengrad/data/__init__.py.reason: Upstream re-exports adapters, materialize, normalize and renderers, none of which are vendored. All vendored modules import siblings absolutely, so an empty package init is sufficient.

runtime_dependencies: pyyaml (opengrad/data/behavior.py module-level import only; DECISIONS itself needs none)
vendoring_rationale: The upstream core declares dependencies = []; a git dependency would make a published benchmark's scorer contingent on a third-party repository staying reachable at a mutable ref. Reimplementation is rejected because parse_qwen_native_output is deliberately byte-compatible with openweights' Kotlin ToolCallParser, and a third copy of a three-way contract has nothing keeping it aligned.
